The story presents distinct, believable responses to the same institutional crisis: Helen’s weary endurance, Marguerite’s health-driven anger, Peter’s strained administrative diplomacy, Arnold’s dismissiveness, and Tomasz’s practical candor. Less sympathetic viewpoints, such as the dean’s budget-focused reasoning and Arnold’s accusation of “hysteria,” fit their roles and circumstances without being endorsed. Though these characters receive less depth than Helen, their contrasting perspectives convincingly reveal the department’s tensions.
